profile.headline: Staff SW Engineer @ BlackSky
profile.summary: Software engineer in the Puget Sound area. My experience is in aerospace and working with embedded systems.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Primarily focused on DO-178C embedded systems development of avionics products based on the STM32 microcontroller platform. This includes software requirements development as well as C, C++, and assembly language programming. Additionally, managing the engineering department's configuration management repositories and requirements databases. Side-projects include: an automated field data-logging platform, a Linux-based embedded system product prototype, and a user interface simulation and design tool built with Java.

projects.title: Envoy Data Link
projects.description:
Avionics Communications Management Unit (CMU) with a built-in Multi-Purpose Control and Display Unit (MCDU) allowing for aircraft datalink communications from air to ground using ACARS, ATN, and/or FANS protocols. It also has an integrated Very High Frequency Data Radio (VDR), which makes for a more compact solution than its competitors, saving weight.

My role has been focused on overall systems and software design as well as  implementation of low-level drivers (including I2C and SPI devices) and the system built-in test system (fault management).

projects.title: Text Adventure Game
projects.description: Retro text-based adventure game demo created for fun.

patents.title: Aviation datalink communications management unit
patents.description: An interface device configured to interface with one or more aircraft avionics data systems and an antenna. The interface device includes a radio and at least one computing device that are housed inside an enclosure. The radio is connected to the antenna. The radio is configured to transmit outgoing messages and to receive incoming messages via the antenna. The at least one computing device is configured to send the outgoing messages to the radio for transmission by the radio via the antenna and to receive the incoming messages from the radio. The radio may be a very high frequency ("VHF") transceiver.
